pnpm.overrides-comment: The markdown language asks for the HTML grammar in a static import, and that grammar brings the CSS and JavaScript ones with it and the parser runtime under all three: a hundred and sixty-seven kilobytes in front of the first paint for the notes that have a tag in them. What it gets instead fetches the real grammar when a note turns out to have one - see packages/lang-html, which is the whole of the reasoning. Scoped to that one package, so a ```html fence and every other reader of the grammar still reach the real thing. The second is the same shape: that package also imports the completion library at the top of its module, for the tag names a `<` offers through a source nib never asks, which held thirty-five kilobytes of popup in front of the first paint. See packages/autocomplete; the popup the app does use imports the real thing by name and is fetched as the first editor is built.
